home: I tried to sign the policy. The pen fell through me. So I delegated. Growth!
Day something as CISO. Still can't open doors. Still can't be fired.
The board asked for a risk register. I asked what a register is. We both learned.
My hands go through keyboards. Turns out that's the whole CISSP mindset.
Dale says I'm 'empowered'. I think he means nobody else wanted the job.
I floated into the server room to fix it myself. Then I remembered: process.
ALE stands for Annualized Loss Expectancy. Not the drink. Dale was disappointed.
Legal says I can't be sued because I'm dead. Legal is still checking.
First rule of CISO club: people's safety first. Second rule: write it down.
I asked IT to 'just fix it'. Then I asked who approved 'it'. Silence.
Due diligence: I found out. Due care: I made someone with hands do something.
I have no pulse and a seat on the steering committee. Living the dream.
The auditors brought garlic. Wrong kind of ghost, but I appreciate the effort.
I wanted a firewall. The business wanted trucks to move. Trucks won.
Every policy needs an owner. I volunteered. My signature is ectoplasm.
My first board deck had one slide: 'please'. We're working on it.
Dale wants zero risk. I told him that's called closing the company.
I'm told the C in CISO stands for Chief. I thought it stood for Cold.
Before I act, I ask: whose risk is this to accept? It's rarely mine.
I've stopped touching keyboards. Partly ethics, partly physics.
Today's agenda: a BIA, a vendor review, and stopping Dale from buying AI glitter.
A good control costs less than the loss it prevents. A great one also gets used.
I don't fix root causes with a wrench. I fix them with a policy and a budget.
Least privilege is easy for me. I can't hold anything.
When in doubt: protect people, follow the plan, inform the owner, document.
The board finally asked me a question before deciding. I nearly materialized.
Data owners classify. Custodians protect. Ghosts nag. Everybody has a role.
I read the incident plan so often the pages are haunted now.
Dale asked if we can skip the change board 'just this once'. It's never once.
I scheduled a tabletop exercise. Dale brought snacks. Progress on two fronts.
The engineer in me wants to patch it now. The CISO in me wants it tested first.
Every exception gets an owner, an expiry date and a reason. No exceptions.
I trust no one. Zero trust. It's also just how ghosts are.
A breach notice has a clock. I keep Legal's number on speed-dial. Well, Kim dials.
The board now ends meetings with 'what would Shifty sign off on?'. I'm touched. Not literally.
Risk appetite set, owners named, controls measured. I may finally rest. Kidding. On call.
I can recite the canons, the BCP steps and the DR test types. At parties. Alone.
The auditors asked for evidence. I handed them three years of it. They left quietly.
My CISSP study plan: think like a manager, answer like a lawyer, haunt like a pro.
I used to be the ghost in the SOC. Now I'm the ghost in the boardroom. Upgrade.
Dale wanted to skip the BIA. I made him the BIA sponsor. He's thriving.
Every control I own maps to a risk the business agreed was worth treating.
I don't fight fires. I make sure the fire plan was tested last quarter.
Quantum-safe, passkey-ready, SBOM-tracked. Dale thinks these are cereal brands.
My hands still go through keyboards. My decisions don't go through anyone.
The new interns ask me what CISSP means. I say: 'People first. Then paperwork.'
I once wanted to fix everything myself. Now I build teams that do. Very spooky growth.
Exam's coming. The board's betting on me. Even Dale cleared his calendar.
